paper.title: November 2018 Mathematics SL Paper 1
paper.subject: Mathematics SL
paper.solution_status: Independent worked solutions — checked against the official IB markscheme

questions.accessible_text:
1. [Maximum mark: 6]

A circle has centre A and radius 6 cm. [Diagram not to scale: B,C,D lie on circle; minor sector BAC is shaded and ∠BAC=2 radians.]
(a) Find the area of the shaded sector. [2]
(b) Find the perimeter of the non-shaded sector ABDC. [4]
questions.solution: (a) (1/2)(6²)(2)=36 cm². (b) Major arc length=6(2π−2)=12π−12; add two radii to get 12π cm.

questions.accessible_text:
3. [Maximum mark: 6]

In an arithmetic sequence, u₁=−5 and d=3.
(a) Find u₈. [2]
(b) Find n for which uₙ=67. [4]

4. [Maximum mark: 6]

Let b=log₂a, where a>0. Write each expression in terms of b.
(a) log₂(a³) [2]
(b) log₂(8a) [2]
(c) log₈a [2]

5. [Maximum mark: 6]

Consider vectors a=(3,2p) and b=(p+1,8). Find possible p for which a and b are parallel.
questions.solution: Parallel components satisfy 3/(p+1)=2p/8. Cross-multiplying gives 24=2p(p+1), so p²+p−12=0=(p+4)(p−3). Therefore p=−4 or p=3.

questions.accessible_text:
6. [Maximum mark: 8]

Let f(x)=(6−2x)/√(16+6x−x²). [Diagram: the graph of f encloses region R with the x- and y-axes.] Find the area of R.
questions.solution: The x-intercept is x=3. Since d(16+6x−x²)/dx=6−2x, ∫₀³f(x)dx=[2√(16+6x−x²)]₀³=2(5)−2(4)=2.

questions.accessible_text:
7. [Maximum mark: 6]

Given sin x=1/3, where 0<x<π/2, find cos4x.

8. [Maximum mark: 16]

Let f(x)=x²−4x−5. [Diagram: part of the upward-opening parabola.]
(a) Find the x-intercepts. [5]
(b) Find the axis of symmetry. [2]
(c) f(x)=(x−h)²+k. (i) Write h. (ii) Find k. [4]
The graph of g is obtained by reflecting f in the y-axis, then translating by vector (−3,6).
(d) Find the vertex of g. [5]
questions.solution: (a) (x−5)(x+1)=0, so x=−1,5. (b) x=2. (c) h=2,k=−9. (d) Vertex (2,−9) reflects to (−2,−9), then translates to (−5,−3).

questions.accessible_text:
9. [Maximum mark: 15]

A bag contains n marbles, two blue. Hayley draws without replacement until drawing blue.
(a) Find, in terms of n, probability game ends on (i) first draw; (ii) second draw. [4]
(b) Let n=5. Find probability it ends on (i) third; (ii) fourth draw. [4]
She pays $20. [Table: draws 1,2,3,4; money back $M: 0,20,8k,12k.]
(c) Find k for a fair game. [7]

10. [Maximum mark: 16]

Let f(x)=x³−2x²+ax+6. [Diagram: graph crosses y-axis at P; line L tangent there; local minimum Q lies on L.]
(a) Find P. [2]
(b) (i) Find f′(x). (ii) Hence find L in terms of a. [6]
(c) Find a. [8]
questions.summary: Use tangent and stationary point conditions.
questions.solution: (a) P=(0,6). (b) f′=3x²−4x+a; at P slope a, so L:y=ax+6. (c) Intersections satisfy x³−2x²+ax+6=ax+6, so x²(x−2)=0 and Q has x=2. As Q is a minimum, f′(2)=12−8+a=0, hence a=−4.
